Rumors have long suggested that Apple is designing a brand new all-glass iPhone for its 20th anniversary next year. However, one Jefferies analyst thinks the device will no longer move forward.

A Wall Street analyst says the 20th anniversary iPhone redesign has been canceled

Wall Street firm Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating to "underperform" today, with analyst Edison Lee pointing out that a potential cancelation of the 20th anniversary iPhone redesign is one of the main reasons for the move.

The key to today's downgrade lies in rumors that Apple's all-glass iPhone project has been canceled. Although the project was reported as early as 2025 to be in development, with rumors suggesting a launch as soon as 2027, Apple has never commented on these rumors. However, the company quietly filed a patent for a "six-sided glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies had previously thought that launching an all-glass iPhone was reasonable and feasible, but Lee believes development work has come to a halt. According to the analyst, supply chain checks indicate that the project was canceled due to low yield rates. Lee views this decision as "a major setback for pushing higher-priced iPhones amid soaring memory costs." Had the device launched as planned in September 2027 to commemorate the iPhone's 20th anniversary, he estimated the blended retail price would reach $2,060—higher than the average price of any previous model. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further driving up their average selling price and profit margins." He sees this as an important defensive strategy in an environment of rising memory prices.

Lee also pointed to Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro as additional reasons for the further downgrade of the company's stock.

It is unclear from Lee's report whether the analyst means the entire major redesign has been shelved, or only some design elements have been canceled.

The top-rated comment was posted by Currentinterest

These analysts have been wrong many times in their predictions about Apple's future plans. The term "all-glass" may not even accurately reflect what Apple truly intends to do. The 20th anniversary phone will be innovative, and whatever the final design looks like, it will sell like hotcakes.

For example, there have long been rumors that Apple will not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an "all-glass" display will not be possible. However, the rumored quad-curved design may still be adopted.

In any case, if the Apple iPhone 20th anniversary design has indeed been canceled, we should soon receive confirmation from other reliable sources.
